subject: Throughput profiling & autoscale guidelines for ACME private GPU pool
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput profiling & autoscale guidelines for ACME private GPU pool

Sara / ACME ops team —

Thanks for the details on the private deployment. Before we kick off a sizing run, a few concrete asks so our profiling and autoscale recommendations line up with your expectations: 

- Workload mix: please confirm the approximate split between short chat sessions (~25-50 tokens per turn), long-form summarization (500+ tokens), and embedding/vector requests. Sample traces are most useful.
- Target SLOs: you mentioned wanting to keep p95 generation latency under 350ms. Can you confirm p50/p90 goals and acceptable tail behavior during 10-minute spikes?
- Spike profile: we need expected peak magnitude and duration (e.g., 3.5k rps for 10 minutes).
- Network constraints: any egress caps in the VPC, preferred peering method (TGW, PrivateLink), and whether we can establish a dedicated cross-connect for sustained throughput.
- Security: do you require KMS at rest (customer-managed) and mTLS for control-plane?

Once we have traces I’ll schedule a profiling job against a quantized model family variant and produce a short sizing sheet: baseline GPUs, warm-pool targets, and an autoscale policy that balances cost and headroom. Our initial baseline assumptions (subject to confirmation): sustained throughput target 1,200 rps; spike to 3,500 rps for ~10 minutes; p95 latency 350ms; allow 30% headroom for warmups and KV cache misses.

Attached: a quick template you can drop traces into (acme_workload_sample.json). If you prefer, send a subset of production logs and we’ll anonymize and run internally.

Would like to run the first profile tomorrow afternoon (PDT) if we get traces this morning.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Date: 2026-08-12T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput profiling & autoscale guidelines for ACME private GPU pool

Michael —

Thanks, sending a sanitized trace and our target profile. High level:
- Workload mix (approx): chat generation 60% (avg 35 tokens/response), long-form summarization 25% (avg 800 tokens), embeddings 15% (batch embeddings requests).
- Targets: sustained 1,200 rps (requests/sec), p50 90ms, p95 350ms, p99 allowed up to 900ms during spikes.
- Spikes: we see traffic bursts up to ~3,500 rps lasting 6–12 minutes, ~3x baseline, typically driven by marketing launches.
- Network: VPC peered via Transit Gateway to our infra; egress allocation for the Redwoods endpoint currently 10 Gbps but can be increased after procurement approval. We prefer AWS Direct Connect for the cross-connect long-term.
- Security: customer-managed KMS required for keys; control-plane traffic must be restricted to our management hosts via mTLS.

Attached: acme_workload_trace_2026-07.json (sanitized), and a short diagram of our VPC egress topology.

Sara Jenkins
Head of Production Ops, Acme Corporation
sara.jenkins@acme.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-13T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput profiling & autoscale guidelines for ACME private GPU pool

Folks —

We ran a quick pass on Sara’s trace overnight. High-level sizing and recommended autoscale levers below. I’ve attached a one-page estimate and a sketch of an autoscale policy.

Sizing summary (preliminary):
- Model: opt-6.9b-quant-4 (profiled variant)
- Baseline sustained: 1,200 rps -> ~12 x A100 80GB-equivalent GPUs (continuous batching + KV cache benefits applied)
- Spike headroom: to absorb 3,500 rps short bursts we recommend an autoscale ceiling of 20 x A100 eq (reserve burst capacity or accept briefly elevated latency during cold starts)
- Warm pool: maintain a warm pool equal to ~25% of baseline (3 GPUs) to reduce KV-cache cold misses on scaled-up instances
- Batching: steady-state batch size 4; micro-batch concurrency 8 across each worker; batching window 8–12ms to keep p95 under 350ms for chat-like traffic
- Network: recommend provisioning 12–15 Gbps per rack to avoid egress throttling at peak; ensure MTU tuning for large token payloads
- Quantization: 4-bit quant reduces memory and improves packing, giving ~1.6x throughput improvement vs fp16 in our microbenchmarks; we expect this to be a safe production variant but will validate accuracy on your eval set

Autoscale policy (short):
- Metric: combined token throughput + queue depth (token_rate per GPU)
- Scale-up: immediate add of 1 node when token_rate > 75% of node capacity for 30s; aggressive add up to 3 nodes within 2 minutes if sustained
- Scale-down: remove nodes when token_rate < 40% for 10 minutes and warm pool maintained
- Warm-pool behavior: keep 3 pre-warmed nodes during business hours, allow scale-down to 2 overnight

Operational notes / risks:
- KV cache warmup: long-form summarization results in larger KV caches; cache warm-up can cause higher latency on scale-up. Warm pool mitigates this but we should plan a short degradation window on major rollouts.
- Burst billing: if procurement can't approve dedicated cross-connect now, cost of running additional burst capacity over public interconnect may be higher — flag for finance.
- Observability: we’ll push a per-shard token throughput metric to your CloudWatch namespace and enable tracing for 1 hour during the next test to validate p99 behavior.

Attachments: sizing-estimate.xlsx (detailed numbers + cost estimate), autoscale-policy.yaml (candidate policy for orchestration).

If this looks reasonable I recommend a 30–45 minute walkthrough with Acme ops and networking to sign off on the egress/connect plan and to schedule the production profiling run (we’ll need a 60–90 minute maintenance window to fully validate warm-pool behavior).

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Sara / team —

Thanks for the trace and the quick turn from Laura. Proposal accepted in principle. Next steps:

1) Schedule a 45-minute technical walkthrough tomorrow (2026-08-14) at 10:00 PDT to align on egress/connect and warm-pool constraints. I’ll send a calendar invite.
2) Procurement: Sara, please confirm whether ACME can provision the Direct Connect / cross-connect; if not, we’ll include the incremental burst cost in the estimate.
3) We’ll run the profile during the approved maintenance window and turn on enhanced tracing for 60 minutes to capture p99 behavior.

I’ll attach the invite and the two files from Laura in the calendar invite. Appreciate the quick collaboration — we’ll tighten the sizing after the walkthrough.

Best —
Michael
